newsitem.title: FRANCE: French stocks end with narrow gains.
newsitem.headline: French stocks end with narrow gains.

text.p: French shares finished barely higher after trading in a 20-point range during the day.

Traders said the market was still consolidating but falls were limited by buying on the first day of the new account. Dollar weakness against the mark and softer bond markets also weighed on the market, which was otherwise livened by sharp rises in Club Med, CLF-Dexia and AGF.
The blue-chip CAC-40 index closed up 5.01 points or 0.2 percent at 2,567.85 while the CAC-40 futures contract was down at 2,570 from 2,577 on Friday's close.

* Club Mediterranee rose 21.24 percent to 431 francs. The stock was suspended limit up twice in the morning, after the market went on buying frenzy on news that Euro Disney chairman Philippe Bourguignon will head the group.
* CLF-Dexia added 4.92 percent to 533. The Franco-Belgian bank said after the close it was buying 40 percent of Crediop, a unit of Italy's San Paolo di Torino, paying between 1.6-1.9 billion francs.
* AGF rises 5.78 percent, spurred by speculation of a takeover by Allianz of Germany or an aquisition of the Athena unit of Worms. AGF has denied any Athena bid plans.

* Worms et Cie chairman Jean-Philippe Thierry said it is considering Athena's future in view of the big changes in the insurance world. Worms ended down six percent at 388, hit by profit-taking after rising 10 percent on Friday.
* Saint-Louis finished down 0.86 percent at 1,492, after hitting a historic high in the day of 1,534, on the back of the premium on its planned Worms merger.
* Eramet closed down 11.86 percent at 270, dented by news the government is withdrawing mining rights at the Koniambo plant in New Caledonia.
* The Channel Tunnel operator said its bank syndicate had agreed to extend its debt standstill until December 14.

A Eurotunnel spokeswoman said the firm still hoped to conclude restructuring details by end of March to allow a prospectus to be sent to shareholders in early April so they can vote on the package by the end of June.
